questions.problem: Given that ${lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{{6}^{x}-4}{{3}^{x}+c}=4,$ what is the value of constant $c?$
questions.worked_solution:
We can evaluate this limit in terms of the constant $c$ using direct substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{{6}^{x}-4}{{3}^{x}+c} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to 2}({6}^{x}-4)}{{lim}_{x\to 2}({3}^{x}+c)} \\  & =\frac{{6}^{2}-4}{{3}^{2}+c} \\  & =\frac{32}{9+c}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the above limit is equal to $4,$ we can equate the above with $4,$ and then solve for $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{32}{9+c} & =4 \\ 9+c & =8 \\ c & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

We can evaluate this limit using direct substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}{4}^{x/2} & ={4}^{2/2} \\  & ={4}^{1} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

We can evaluate this limit in terms of the constant $c$ using direct substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{5}^{x}+c}{{2}^{x}-1} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to 1}({5}^{x}+c)}{{lim}_{x\to 1}({2}^{x}-1)} \\  & =\frac{{5}^{1}+c}{{2}^{1}-1} \\  & =\frac{5+c}{2-1} \\  & =\frac{5+c}{1} \\  & =5+c\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the above limit is equal to $4,$ we can equate the above with $4,$ and then solve for $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5+c & =4 \\ c & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that ${lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{4}^{x}-c}{3\cdot {2}^{x}}=2$, what is the value of constant $c?$
questions.worked_solution:
We can evaluate this limit in terms of the constant $c$ using direct substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{4}^{x}-c}{3\cdot {2}^{x}} & =\frac{{4}^{0}-c}{3\cdot {2}^{0}} \\  & =\frac{1-c}{3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the above limit is equal to $2,$ we can equate the above with $2,$ and then solve for $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-c}{3} & =2 \\ 1-c & =6 \\ -c & =6-1 \\ c & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

We can evaluate this limit using direct substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{{3}^{x}+5}{{2}^{x}-3} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to 2}({3}^{x}+5)}{{lim}_{x\to 2}({2}^{x}-3)} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}+5}{{2}^{2}-3} \\  & =\frac{9+5}{4-3} \\  & =\frac{14}{1} \\  & =14\end{aligned}
$$

$$
